control module which also functions as an event data recorder. the data indicates unit 1 was traveling at 51 miles per hour when it crashed into unit 2 and the brakes were not being applied at any of transportation to included the results of an analysis of unit 4's blood. the report is now complete.

records.public_safe_text: this is dallas police traffic fatality # 130 for the year 2020. see related offense report [phone]. unit 1 [roadway]. unit 2 was legally parked and unoccupied along the west curb in front of the residence at [roadway]. unit 3 was legally parked and unoccupied in front of the residence at [roadway]. unit 4, a pedestrian, was on the [roadway] near the right back quarter of unit 3. unit 1 was speeding over the limit when it collided front right to the back left of unit 2 with enough force to propel unit 2 forward where it struck the concrete curb in front of [roadway]. unit 2, which was in a counterclockwise rotation, collided front right to the back left of unit 3. at some point in the crash, probably as it struck the concrete curb, the right front wheel, tire and brake rotor of unit 2 broke free from unit 2 in one piece. according to a witness, the wheel, tire and brake rotor assembly struck unit 4. unit 1, which was in a clockwise rotation, collided with the metal fence which bordered the front yard of [roadway]. the driver of unit 1 fled the scene on foot failing to make any attempt to render aid to and/or summon aid for unit 4 [medical facility] by dallas fire rescue ambulance, but succumbed to injuries suffered in the crash. he was pronounced deceased at 3:[medical facility] physician [medical facility] staff. a detective from the dallas police vehicle crimes unit responded to the scene as did a traffic sergeant. a laser scan of the scene was done. the report has been marked incomplete pending an analysis of a specimen of unit 4's blood. there is no evidence that the driver of unit 1 took any evasive action, such as braking, to avoid or mitigate the severity of the crash. the driver of unit 1 has no driver license and has not demonstrated that he has the knowledge or skill necessary to safely operate a motor vehicle. on october 16, 2020 a search warrant was executed to obtain crash data from unit 1's power train control module which also functions as an event data recorder. the data indicates unit 1 was traveling at 51 miles per hour when it crashed into unit 2 and the brakes were not being applied at any time during the recording period of the data. the speed limit on the roadway were the crash occurred is 35 miles per hour. on [date] this report was supplemented at the request of the texas department of transportation to included the results of an analysis of unit 4's blood. the report is now complete.
